key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell architectures and pinpoint the most influential layer properties for high-efficiency design.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical screening strategy for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations that can boost device performance while reducing costly exhaustive simulation and experiment.
method: Generated 125 device architectures from 5 ETLs, 5 absorbers, and 5 HTLs.
Used a representative subset of SCAPS-1D results to train an ML model for PCE prediction and ranking.
Applied SHAP analysis to identify the most important descriptors and verify top candidates with full SCAPS-1D simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong rank-correlation performance, and the model identified devices reaching 28.85% PCE in full SCAPS-1D verification.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the representativeness of the simulated training subset, so transfer to new materials or processing conditions should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
